title: docs: finish objectui#9297 — schema-rendering.md stops teaching silence, and the expression sandbox states its real allowlist
body:
Fixes #9297.

⭐ This is the **first** PR on this card entitled to a closing keyword. The `⛔ 不用关闭关键词`
in the maintainer's option-A ruling bound PR objectui#9376, which deliberately carried only the
first half; this one finishes the job, and my own measurement below says nothing of the card
remains. Every other card number in this body is kept away from any closing keyword on purpose —
the parser does not read sentences.

⚠️ JSX tag shapes are spelled out in words below — a tag-shaped fragment does not survive a GitHub
body field, and the passages this work is about are exactly JSX elements.

Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_011QreXiyMEqKLN4U5daMPVa` — written as prose because a
markdown-link footer does not survive an edit to this body.

## The card had two halves. One was already done; this PR does the other.

**Half one — the three surfaces the dispatch sent me to repair — was already on `main`.** PR
objectui#9376 rewrote them, merged 2026-09-13 as `035d3fac31`, an ancestor of my base
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 0, which self-proves on a shallow checkout). I re-measured
rather than inherit that, because a dead premise reported as work done is the failure mode here.

**Half two — `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md` — is what this card stayed open for**, per
the maintainer's option-A ruling, and it is what this PR repairs.

## Half one, re-measured at my own head, with a lit control

Matched SchemaRenderer elements **with a word boundary after the name**, so SchemaRendererProvider
— the *correct* carrier — is excluded by construction, and the element count is reported so an
empty offender list is a reading rather than a silent zero.

| surface | elements | forwarded look-alikes | bare `${…}` heads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content/docs/guide/expressions.md` | 3 | **0** | 28 |
| `content/docs/guide/architecture.md` | 1 | **0** | 2 |
| `README.md` (repo root) | 2 | **0** | 9 |

### The control varies only the claim, never the instrument

The identical script over `035d3fac31^`, the tree immediately before objectui#9376:

| | tag-shaped hits | real elements | look-alikes | bare heads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `035d3fac31^` (pre-repair) | **18** | 15 | **6** (3 / 1 / 2) | 49 |
| my head | 15 | 15 | **0** | 47 |

⇒ the instrument finds all six look-alikes, split across the surfaces exactly as the card reported,
so **zero at my head is a reading**. A second, differently shaped instrument agrees: grepping for
the three prop spellings finds every survivor on a correct carrier or in prose, and lights up on
the pre-repair bytes at expressions 166/544/660, architecture 158 and README 99/275.

All 39 remaining openings on those three surfaces were read and judged **OUT** — published by the
page itself, the reader's own published root under a page that has established the channel, prose
*about* a name, a JS built-in, or the custom evaluation context the page teaches on purpose
(`formatCurrency`, the card's own example).

## Half two — the repair, on `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`

### Item seven: the page taught a silence that is not there

The Data Context paragraph claimed an unresolvable expression means
"nothing throws and **nothing warns**". Nothing throws is right. Nothing warns is not:
`reportEvaluationFault` falls through to `console.warn` whenever the caller supplies no `onFault`
— **no dev-only gate, no `NODE_ENV` read** — and the `evaluator.evaluate(...)` call sites in
`SchemaRenderer.tsx` that resolve authored text all pass no options. Re-verified at this head
rather than inherited.

The page stated it **twice** (the second sentence taught the same silence by omission), so both
move, and both now carry **the phrasing the expression guide already publishes** rather than new
wording — which is the point, because the two guides currently disagree in writing.

### The six bare-head sites, judged one at a time

⭐ Re-derived at my own head, not trusted from the earlier reading.

| site | head | verdict | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:242`, `:243` | `status` | **IN** | the example calls itself a record — its own description reads "This record is in use" — and a row field's only spelling is `record.*`. The bare shorthand and the wrong-layer `data.status` were both retired on runtime record surfaces (objectui#5330 phase 2). Moved to `record.status`. |
| `:490` | `loading` | OUT | host state the reader publishes; nothing in ObjectUI owns the name |
| `:500` | `items` | OUT | the reader's own collection; the sibling guide teaches the identical Empty State example the same way |
| `:515`, `:517` | `error` | OUT | host state the reader publishes |

⚠️ **The four OUT sites are wrong only under the card's stale reading**, and the card's own
mechanism paragraph is the stale part: it lists `data` as an evaluator root, which objectui#9308
option B removed at the renderer tier — verified in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`, where
the absence is commented as the decision. Under the closed root set those four look like offenders;
under the open one — every key the host publishes is a root — they are ordinary published names.
That is the same rule that left thirty-two sites bare on the sibling surfaces, so calling these
four wrong would contradict the repair this card's own first PR already shipped.

Two further openings on that page, outside the card's six, were judged and left: `stats` at `:71`
is published in the page's own scope object, and `data` at `:127` is prose *about* the root
objectui#9308 removed.

## Also in this PR: one bounded repair of the same class

Found while doing the per-site read. `content/docs/guide/expressions.md`, "Sandboxed Execution",
promised access to "Built-in JavaScript functions (Math, Date, String, Array methods)". Measured
against `SafeExpressionParser`, with a harness control that fired:

| expression | result |
|---|---|
| `${Math.round(average)}` | `2` — promised, works |
| `${Date.now()}` | **ReferenceError: Date is not defined** — promised, fails |
| `${String(average)}` | **TypeError: "String" is not a function** — promised, fails |
| `${Array.isArray(x)}` | **ReferenceError: Array is not defined** — promised, fails |
| `${new Date().getFullYear()}` | `2026` — the spelling the Date Functions section shows, works |
| `${JSON.stringify(x)}` | the array text — works, and was **not** listed |
| `${average + 1}` | `2.5` — HARNESS CONTROL, so the three throws are readings |

`SAFE_GLOBALS` holds `Math`, `JSON`, `parseInt`, `parseFloat`, `isNaN` and `isFinite`; a bare
identifier outside it raises inside the parser, this surface fails soft, and the template comes
back as its own source text. The bullet was wrong in **both** directions. The replacement names the
allowlist *and* points at the constant that defines it, so a later reader re-derives it instead of
trusting a transcribed answer (AGENTS.md #9).
